title: Backflow preventer parts: find the exact assembly before searching components
description: Parts search starts with the exact assembly and failed component.
prompt: Which component is needed and how can it be matched responsibly?
answer: Parts search starts with the exact assembly and failed component. A body, cover, check, relief component, seal, shutoff, test cock, or union can require different sources, procedures, and replacement decisions.
urgency: Do not buy parts from a generic category name or visual resemblance. Escalate obsolete, damaged, or unidentifiable assemblies.
identifiers: Manufacturer, model, and nominal size are required for reliable parts matching.
The observed symptom must be separated from the component identified by a qualified diagnosis.
External piping and shutoff work may fall outside an internal parts kit.

choices.label: I know the model and size
choices.detail: Use model-specific sources before ordering parts or accepting a repair scope.

choices.label: The assembly is leaking or failed
choices.detail: Document the location and obtain a qualified diagnosis before repair.

choices.label: The body may be damaged
choices.detail: Compare repair with a complete replacement and retest scope.

steps.body: Record the label, size, and failed-test or diagnostic finding.

steps.body: Use official literature to match the component family and service scope.

steps.title: Close the risk loop
steps.body: Compare part-only work with a complete repair or replacement scope including retest.
